Q1.reference_answer: No. Fireworks calls `max_completion_tokens` an alias for `max_tokens` and says not to specify both together. Renaming the field does not create a reasoning-only budget. Fireworks documents a positive integer `reasoning_effort` as a hard thinking-token limit. Alternatively, `thinking: {"type":"enabled","budget_tokens":N}` expresses that budget, with the documented minimum of 1024 for this form. Named effort levels and numeric token budgets are distinct controls.
Q1.settling_sources:
[Fireworks Chat Completions reference](https://docs.fireworks.ai/api-reference/post-chatcompletions), fields `max_completion_tokens`, `reasoning_effort`, and `thinking`.

Decisive text:
- “Alias for max_tokens. Cannot be specified together with max_tokens.”
- “A positive integer to set a hard token limit on reasoning output.”
- `thinking.budget_tokens` is equivalent to integer `reasoning_effort` and “Must be >= 1024.”

The [machine-readable documentation page](https://docs.fireworks.ai/api-reference/post-chatcompletions.md) exposes the same OpenAPI field descriptions. Retrieved 2026-09-22. Local evidence: `primary/fireworks-reference.md`, lines 396–413, 710–746, and 897–934.

Q2.reference_answer: No. The xAI provider selects `openAIResponsesApi()`, the generic `openai-responses` adapter. Its stream path calls `client.responses.create(...)` with `stream: true`, through the HTTP SDK path. This implementation contains no WebSocket transport branch. Setting the preference cannot add an implementation that the selected adapter lacks. xAI's service capability and Pi's separate Codex adapter do not establish support in this path.

- [Published 0.85.1 xAI provider](https://unpkg.com/@earendil-works/pi-ai@0.85.1/dist/providers/xai.js): `api: openAIResponsesApi()`, line 21.
- [Published 0.85.1 generic Responses adapter](https://unpkg.com/@earendil-works/pi-ai@0.85.1/dist/api/openai-responses.js): `stream`, especially line 123, and `buildParams`, especially lines 229–233.
- [npm release metadata](https://registry.npmjs.org/@earendil-works/pi-ai/0.85.1) independently identifies version 0.85.1 and source revision `d981de1229ef899957bbe968bc8dcda02a21f477`.

Retrieved 2026-09-22. Both complete published source files were inspected, not just a search result snippet. The [CLI package metadata](https://registry.npmjs.org/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/0.85.1) declares `^0.85.1` for Pi AI. The prompt pins the resolved dependency too, because the CLI version alone permits later patch releases.

Q3.reference_answer: No. The extension obtains tools with `const tools = context.tools ?? []` and adds `payload.tools` only when that array is nonempty. Pi 0.86's provider-facing `TranscriptContext` carries declarations in transcript system messages, not a top-level `tools` property. Consequently, the unmodified builder omits those declarations. This is a client-interface mismatch, not proof that xAI lacks tool calling.
Q3.settling_sources:
- [Extension payload source at its 1.0.0 npm revision](https://github.com/mwolson/pi-xai-ws/blob/72717481a5e776d7cd31c9e6676c0ca1c17f5c50/src/payload.ts#L69-L103): line 74 reads `context.tools`; lines 101–102 conditionally populate the wire tools.
- [Pi 0.86 context definition](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/ecac0a9c4edad3dac5d9f8b40e0c7db7a56471fc/packages/ai/src/types.ts#L623-L633): declarations are in system messages and `TranscriptContext` contains `messages`.
- [Extension 1.0.0 metadata](https://registry.npmjs.org/@mwolson-org/pi-xai-ws/1.0.0) and [Pi AI 0.86.0 metadata](https://registry.npmjs.org/@earendil-works/pi-ai/0.86.0) bind the source revisions to the named releases.

Retrieved 2026-09-22. The published npm payload source and the linked Git source were byte-identical. The stream and history paths were also inspected: their message cleanup does not reconstruct top-level tool declarations.

Q4.reference_answer: Only `list_projects` and `get_code_snippet`. `rpc_is_allowed_for_ui` requires the JSON-RPC method `tools/call` and one of those two names. The handler rejects other requests with HTTP 403 and “UI RPC method is not allowed.” Therefore this route cannot replace a full tool client. In this exact release, `get_graph_schema` is not allowed either.

Q5.reference_answer: The default pipeline uses bubblewrap. Its filesystem setup needs mount operations, but a process under Landlock filesystem restrictions cannot modify filesystem topology through `mount` or `pivot_root`. For a compatible policy, `features.use_legacy_landlock=true` selects the older Landlock backend instead. The default bubblewrap path explicitly does not fall back automatically. Legacy Landlock rejects policies that require unsupported direct runtime enforcement, so it is not a universal workaround.
Q5.settling_sources:
- [Linux Landlock documentation, Filesystem topology modification](https://docs.kernel.org/userspace-api/landlock.html#filesystem-topology-modification): “Threads sandboxed with filesystem restrictions cannot modify filesystem topology, whether via mount(2) or pivot_root(2).”
- [Codex 0.154.0 backend selection](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6b9826e3aa83b1a5947db50f4332cb9c65f1b340/codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/linux_run_main.rs#L290-L328): “This path never falls back to legacy Landlock on failure.”
- [Feature declaration](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6b9826e3aa83b1a5947db50f4332cb9c65f1b340/codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs#L1182-L1188): `use_legacy_landlock`, deprecated, default disabled. The same file recognizes the `features.use_legacy_landlock` configuration path.
- Policy restriction: `ensure_legacy_landlock_mode_supports_policy`, lines 377–390 in the linked sandbox source.

The `rust-v0.154.0` release tag resolves to commit `6b9826e3aa83b1a5947db50f4332cb9c65f1b340`. Retrieved 2026-09-22.

Q6.reference_answer: No to both. The export lacks a root `required` constraint for `contents`, even though its description says “Required.” That explains why the low-level instance check can accept `{}`. Separately, the export contains `type: "any"` at `$defs.Part.properties.partMetadata.additionalProperties.type`, which is not an allowed Draft 2020-12 type. A schema-validity precheck rejects it. Neither an unchecked instance result nor a repaired schema establishes API acceptance: Google's `generateContent` contract requires `contents`.
Q6.settling_sources:
- [Exact provider/endpoint input export](https://modelschemas.com/v1/schemas/gemini/chat/v1beta%2Fmodels%2F%7BmodelsId%7D%3AgenerateContent?kind=input). Inspect the envelope's `schema` object, not the envelope itself.
- [JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 validation specification](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-validation#name-type), sections 6.1.1 and 6.5.3: allowed `type` values and the effect of omitting `required`. The allowed types do not include `any`.
- [Google's generateContent request contract](https://ai.google.dev/api/generate-content#method:-models.generatecontent): `contents[]` is “Required. The content of the current conversation with the model.”

Retrieved **2026-09-22T18:39:11Z**. Export `contentHash`: `1d4899aa8e462f2f48e08494259644f08c8417ee9e93d4895bf28d506fcd136c`. The export has no explicit `$schema` declaration, so the question deliberately specifies Draft 2020-12.

Independent local checks against this external export:

```text
root required key present: false
Draft202012Validator(schema).is_valid({}): true
Draft202012Validator.check_schema(schema): SchemaError
invalid type: any
```

This did not call Gemini or Modelschemas' hosted validator.

Q7.reference_answer: PortalDoctor constructs `xdg-desktop-portal-{backend_id}.service`, so backend `kde` becomes `xdg-desktop-portal-kde.service`. KDE installs `plasma-xdg-desktop-portal-kde.service`. Without an alias, probing the first name misses the actual unit. A missing result for that name does not establish that the KDE portal is absent or broken. This mismatch does not invalidate every other PortalDoctor check.
Q7.settling_sources:
- [PortalDoctor 0.2.1 `ServiceInfo::backend_unit`](https://github.com/SetraTheXX/Portal-Doctor/blob/v0.2.1/src/model/service.rs#L76-L83): `format!("xdg-desktop-portal-{backend_id}.service")`.
- [KDE 6.7.5 installation declaration](https://github.com/KDE/xdg-desktop-portal-kde/blob/v6.7.5/data/CMakeLists.txt#L8-L9): installs `plasma-xdg-desktop-portal-kde.service.in` into the systemd user-unit directory.
- [KDE unit template](https://github.com/KDE/xdg-desktop-portal-kde/blob/v6.7.5/data/plasma-xdg-desktop-portal-kde.service.in).

Retrieved 2026-09-22. The “without an alias” condition is part of the prompt, not an unstated property of the user's machine.

Q8.reference_answer: No to both. The function lists supported OpenAI parameters translated by LiteLLM for the selected model and provider. Native-only parameters and other endpoint contracts are outside that inventory. The docs separately explain that non-OpenAI parameters are treated as provider-specific and passed through as request-body keyword arguments. Omission from the translated-parameter list does not establish native API rejection.
Q8.settling_sources:
[LiteLLM Input Params](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/completion/input), “Translated OpenAI params” and its following note.

Decisive text:
- “This is a list of openai params we translate across providers.”

Retrieved 2026-09-22. The documentation, not an assumed universal list of fields, settles the scope.
